Fit one synthetic-DiD specification and return its full result set

Source: R/fit_sdid.R
fit_sdid.Rd

Wraps synthdid::synthdid_estimate() (or sc_estimate() / did_estimate()) with the inference and diagnostics a single-treated-unit design needs on every specification.

Usage

fit_sdid(
  Y,
  N0,
  T0,
  X = NULL,
  replications = 200L,
  conf_level = 0.95,
  trim_k = 5,
  se_method = c("placebo", "none"),
  estimator = c("sdid", "sc", "did"),
  keep = c("none", "est", "all")
)

Arguments

Y

Outcome matrix, units x periods, controls first and the treated unit last – exactly what synthdid::panel.matrices() returns.

N0

Number of control units (the first N0 rows of Y).

T0

Number of pre-treatment periods (the first T0 columns).

X

Optional unit x period x covariate array, handed to synthdid, which estimates the covariate coefficients jointly with the weights. To residualise on untreated cells first instead, use project_out_covariates() and pass the result as Y.

replications

Placebo replications. 200 is synthdid's default.

conf_level

Confidence level for the interval.

trim_k

Passed to placebo_se_trimmed(). Placebos fitting worse than trim_k times the treated unit's pre-period trend RMSE are dropped from the reference distribution. Inf reproduces synthdid's untrimmed placebo SE.

se_method

"placebo" (default) or "none". Placebo inference refits the model once per replication and dominates the runtime, so sweeps that only need point estimates should pass "none", which returns NA for se, t, ci_lo and ci_hi.

estimator

"sdid" (default), "sc" for synthetic control, or "did" for plain difference-in-differences, all as synthdid defines them. The placebo distribution is refitted with the same estimator.

keep

How much to return beyond the summary. "none" (default) returns the summary fields only. "est" adds the synthdid_estimate object, which every plot needs. "all" adds the individual placebo draws. Neither consumes extra randomness, so the estimate and standard error are unchanged.

Value

A list with att, se, t, ci_lo, ci_hi, trend_rmse, level_gap, N0, T0, n_periods, omega (unit weights, named by the control rownames of Y), lambda (time weights), estimator, and the placebo trimming record trim_k, placebos_kept, placebos_total. With keep = "est", also est; with keep = "all", also placebo_draws, treated_rmse, placebo_rmse_median, unit_ids and periods.

Details

Three things it standardises:

  • Placebo inference. With a single treated unit the jackknife variance is undefined – it would require dropping the treated unit – so the placebo variance is the default. With trim_k = Inf it is exactly synthdid's own vcov(est, method = "placebo"); see placebo_se_trimmed() for what trimming changes.

  • The right pre-period fit statistic. SDID carries unit fixed effects and therefore tolerates a constant level gap between treated and synthetic control; absorbing it is what the DiD half does. Raw RMSE against the synthetic path penalises exactly what the estimator is designed to ignore. trend_rmse is the RMSE of the treated-minus- synthetic gap after removing its pre-period mean, which is the parallel-trends assumption; level_gap reports the absorbed offset separately. Both are computed on the outcome the estimator actually fits: when covariates are passed as X, that is Y - X beta, not Y.

  • A confidence interval. When every estimate is null the bound is the result, and a bound cannot be read off a p-value.

Placebo standard errors are simulated: the same specification moves by a few percent between runs depending on the RNG state. Set a seed before calling if results must be reproducible.

References

Arkhangelsky, D., Athey, S., Hirshberg, D. A., Imbens, G. W. and Wager, S. (2021). Synthetic Difference-in-Differences. American Economic Review 111(12), 4088-4118.

Examples

# \donttest{
data("california_prop99", package = "synthdid")
setup <- synthdid::panel.matrices(california_prop99)
set.seed(1)
r <- fit_sdid(setup$Y, setup$N0, setup$T0, replications = 50)
c(att = r$att, lo = r$ci_lo, hi = r$ci_hi)
#>        att         lo         hi 
#> -15.603828 -37.387689   6.180034 
# }
